definition: The water temperature close to the ocean surface (typically upper 1mm to a few meters). Measured by Sentinel-3 SLSTR radiometers and NOAA AVHRR. Crucial for identifying thermal fronts, upwelling zones, and tropical cyclone intensity.

The primary photosynthetic pigment in ocean phytoplankton, measured in mg/m³ by OceanSat-3 OCM and Sentinel-3 OLCI. High concentrations signify coastal upwelling and rich feeding grounds for pelagic fish species like Yellowfin Tuna and Mackerel.

Geospatial sectors identified by INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services) combining thermal gradients (SST) and ocean color (Chlorophyll-a) to locate high-density pelagic fish aggregations.
Sovereign maritime border dividing national territorial waters and Exclusive Economic Zones. ORCA enforces a 5nm (9.26 km) automated standoff safety buffer to prevent accidental border violations.

Sea zone prescribed by UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea) extending up to 200 nautical miles from the coastal baseline, over which a sovereign state has special rights regarding exploration and use of marine resources.
Average height of the highest one-third of waves in a given sea state spectrum. Measured in meters by radar altimeters. SWH above 3.5m poses operational hazards for mechanized fishing trawlers.
Wind-driven motion where wind blowing parallel to a coastline combined with Coriolis effect pushes surface water offshore, forcing cold, nutrient-rich deep water to ascend to the photic zone.

Measurement of ocean depth from sea surface to ocean floor. Structural seafloor features like continental shelf breaks (200m contour) create physical upwelling currents favoring demersal and pelagic species.
